titleTag: US Visa Appointment Abu Dhabi & UAE: Slots Open Again
h1: US Visa Appointments in Abu Dhabi and Dubai Are Open Again: How to Get One
deck: Routine visa work in the UAE stopped in March 2026 and has come back in pieces. Nonimmigrant interview appointments are being released again, on a schedule most applicants have never been told about, while immigrant visa services are still shut.
metaDescription: US visa appointments in Abu Dhabi and Dubai are being released again. When new slots appear, which portal the UAE uses, who can apply here, what is still suspended.

coverAlt: US visa interview appointments are being released again in the UAE: Friday mornings between 7:30 and 11:30, booked through usvisascheduling.com, with all immigrant visa services still suspended and the $750 paid expedite not available in the UAE

faq.q: Are US visa appointments available in Abu Dhabi and Dubai right now?
faq.a: Limited nonimmigrant visa appointments are available. The US Mission to the UAE has been on ordered departure since March 2026 and routine visa services were suspended, but the mission's own security messaging now states that limited nonimmigrant visa appointments are available while all immigrant visa services remain suspended. Limited means exactly that: appointments exist, but far fewer of them than a normally staffed post would release, and they are gone quickly.

faq.q: When are new US visa appointment slots released in the UAE?
faq.a: The US Embassy in Abu Dhabi and the US Consulate General in Dubai release nonimmigrant visa interview appointments every Friday morning between 7:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m., US and UAE holidays excepted. The mission also says it may occasionally release additional appointments outside that schedule. This is published by the mission itself, and it is the single most useful fact an applicant in the UAE can know.

faq.q: Which website do I use to book a US visa appointment in the UAE?
faq.a: The UAE uses usvisascheduling.com, not the AIS portal at ais.usvisa-info.com that serves India, Canada and many other countries. The UAE moved to the current contractor's system on 30 May 2025 and the AIS site now states that it no longer provides appointment scheduling for the United Arab Emirates. Guides written for the AIS portal describe screens and reschedule rules that do not exist on the system you will actually be using.

faq.q: Can I fly to Dubai or Abu Dhabi to get an earlier US visa interview?
faq.a: In almost all cases no. Since the State Department's guidance of 6 September 2025, updated on 10 October 2025, nonimmigrant visa applicants are directed to apply in their country of nationality or legal residence. Applicants who schedule outside it are told to expect significantly longer waits and that qualifying may be harder, and fees paid are neither refunded nor transferred. The UAE was one of the most heavily used third country processing destinations in the world before that guidance, which is exactly why it changed.

faq.q: Can I pay the $750 expedite fee in the UAE?
faq.a: No. The State Department's expedited appointment pilot is running only at designated missions, and as of 19 August 2026 those are Mission Mexico and Mission Canada. No post in the UAE participates, so no fee will buy you a faster interview in Abu Dhabi or Dubai. The pilot is scheduled to end on 31 December 2026, and the department has said further locations may be added during the testing period.

faq.q: What can I do if I need an interview sooner than the calendar offers?
faq.a: The UAE posts operate the ordinary expedited appointment process. You first book a regular interview on the earliest date the system will give you, then submit an expedite request explaining the urgency with documentary evidence. It is free, it is discretionary, and it is decided by the consular section rather than by anything you pay. Genuine medical emergencies, funerals of immediate family and unavoidable business travel are the usual grounds. A holiday booking is not.

faq.q: Are immigrant visa and green card interviews happening in the UAE?
faq.a: No. The mission's current position is that all immigrant visa services remain suspended, with no resumption date announced. That is a separate track from nonimmigrant visas and it has not reopened alongside them. If you are in an immigrant visa process at Abu Dhabi, watch the mission's own updates rather than any third party, because nothing anyone outside the government does will move that queue.
